text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape resembled NVDA's current state, the median realised return over the next 5 sessions was 0.86%. The distribution is wide and slightly right-skewed, with a standard deviation of 3.8%, meaning the path over one trading week has historically swung roughly between -4.04% and 4.68% at the 10th and 90th percentiles.

[state]
The engine pulled these specific analogs because several features are elevated simultaneously. WTI crude change, 20 days (oilChg20) is at 19.24%, carrying a z-score of 1.124, which is the most extreme macro feature in the current state. The name itself is volatile: 20-session realised volatility (annualised) (vol20) sits at 45.77% (z-score 0.824), and mean absolute overnight/weekend gap, 20 sessions (gap20) is 1.28% (z-score 0.718). Distance from 52-week high (dist52) is -6.03% (z-score 0.564), confirming the proximity to highs you noted. Calendar days to next earnings release (dte) is capped at 45 days (z-score 0.663), while scheduled event load, next 5 sessions (eventLoad5) is 0 (z-score -0.496). Meanwhile, benchmark 20-session volatility (mktVol20) is quiet at 9.16% (z-score -0.574), and 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) is negative at -0.785 (used as -0.62). This combination of idiosyncratic heat, an oil shock, and a quiet broad market defines the neighbourhood these 50 analogs occupy.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs spanning from 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08, the mean 5-session return was 0.65% and the median was 0.86%. The spread is substantial: the 25th percentile was -2.03% and the 75th percentile was 3.07%. The extremes ranged from -7.34% to 10.25%, with a skew of 0.214. In 56% of the episodes the return was above zero, and in 44% it was below. The bad tail is populated by specific names. The single closest match was NVDA itself on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2999), which went on to realise a -5.9% return over 5 sessions. Another NVDA episode on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.4317) did the opposite, returning 9.66%. XLK on 2026-08-13 (distance 0.4178) returned -4.02%. On the positive side, MU on 2024-01-16 (distance 0.4111) returned 3.45%, and LLY on 2026-08-13 (distance 0.4066) returned 3.08%. The sector breakdown of the analog set leans heavily into Technology (9), Health Care (5), Financials (5), Energy (4), Communication (4), and various ETF sleeves, reflecting the cross-asset nature of the matching features.

[tails]
A position can finish the week near flat but still be un-holdable through the middle. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -2.01%. At the 25th percentile, the worst intra-week drawdown was -3.77%, and at the 10th percentile it was -4.38%. Looking at discrete thresholds, 8 of the 50 episodes breached a 5% drawdown during the 5-session window. None of the 50 episodes breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown. The median max favourable excursion was 2.55%, reaching 4.39% at the 75th percentile and 6.71% at the 90th percentile. The reward-risk ratio computed from these excursions is 1.27.

[stress]
The stress scenarios that materially worsen the baseline median of 0.86% are led by the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash. In those 48 analogs, the median forward return was -5.4%, a delta of -6.26% versus baseline, with a 10th percentile of -14.14% and a 58.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. The caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare produced a median of -3.02% (delta -3.88%) across 50 analogs, with only a 4% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation / rate bear scenario yielded a median of -2.42% (delta -3.28%) across 50 analogs, with a 16% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2025-04 tariff shock showed a median of -2.7% (delta -3.56%) across 26 analogs, with a 19.2% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind gave a median of -2.11% (delta -2.97%) across 36 analogs, with a 16.7% probability of a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. Scenarios like the Volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX), Policy-rate path re-pricing (+1.5 sigma), Liquidity air pocket, Earnings release day, FOMC decision day, Crypto drawdown contagion, China ADR de-rating, and 2023-03 regional bank stress all produced medians closer to the baseline or slightly positive, with deltas ranging from -1.25% to +0.75%. No scenarios were skipped by the engine.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The conformal interval achieves 80.8% out-of-sample coverage with a width of 9.95%, but the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -7.6%, and the directional hit rate is 50.1%. The PIT chi-square statistic is 208.6 against a 5% critical value of 16.92.

Regarding the instrument you would actually trade: the wrapper status is measured. The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 54.59% of the Bitget NVDA/USDT perpetual's own hourly price movement landed in those closed hours. It is classified as a fair tracker with a return correlation of 0.8988 and a tracking error of 111 bp/day. The basis band against the raw close is -0.37% to 0.66%, and the spread is 0.44 bps. The caveat is that this is a 24/7 perpetual, not a redeemable spot token: funding applies, the basis differs from the reference close the analog distribution is built on, and the tracking error carries idiosyncratic risk. Nothing here feeds the retrieval engine or the conformal scale.

For sizing context, the closed-session return layer measured 6 weekend blocks on Bitget. The median weekend block return was 0.428%, the 10th percentile was -1.3695%, and the standard deviation was 1.4103%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.8185%. Zero out of 6 weekends breached a 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
